design: Repeat on two fresh single-thread-per-core AMD Milan n2d-standard-4 guests, CPU 1 with cgroup and affinity. Use the same binaries and current bundle engine for both client revisions. Nine direct user+system CPU completions per case and program.
cost: For each executable and input, compare previous/current cheap profile child CPU using the median paired previous/current ratio from two alternating pairs. Check ordinary counters for both releases and one current four-counter diagnostic. For the historical interwoven control compare against both archived #95 full profiles.
order: For the three new query permutations compare native medians, full counters and query edge totals per executable. Predeclared directional check: shuffled queries take more CPU than ascending queries on each boot. Loop body counts and these semantic step totals do not measure CPU cache misses.
holdout: Hold tiled direct CPU times out of forecasting. On each boot and each ELF use the ascending native median times the ratio of tiled/ascending frozen combined instruction+REP work for the baseline. For the candidate, let x be the sum of the bit lengths of absolute differences between successive queried character positions. Interpolate linearly in x between the native medians for ascending and shuffled on the same executable and boot. Require x(ascending) < x(tiled) < x(shuffled). Round estimates up to integer nanoseconds. The candidate pays for a second endpoint; also report the unweighted mean of the two paid endpoint times as a cost-matched control. Count native TLE only on strict excess. Report signed error, fixed-deadline votes and correct majorities for both held-out executions, separately per boot. Register forecasts before collection and replay them offline.
placement: Keep the image default ASLR setting on both guests. Report observed counter drift and every profile. Use an independent 120-second safety watchdog. All timestamps for cost and forecasts use child wait4 CPU time.
